items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: Ed Thigpen, yes, and of course Kenny Clarke, the late Kenny Clarke, the late Leo Wright who played with Dizzy, and there were some great musicians who got jobs in the studio.

ctx.x: Ed Thigpen, yes, and of course Kenny Clarke, the late Kenny Clarke, the late Leo Wright who played with Dizzy, and there were some great musicians who got jobs in the studio. Herb Geller, an alto saxophonist, white American, he went over there and so did Sal Nistico.
